Elena — thanks for the clear list. Summarizing answers and next steps below; attaching an initial evidence matrix.

Short answers (high-level):
- Wipe artifacts: we can provide a wipe manifest (job ID, start/end timestamps), object deletion manifests (prefix-level deletion list), and an optional signed attestation PDF stamped with our internal run ID and UTC timestamp. For Private/VPC we can surface the job IDs and manifests from the customer-controlled storage layer where the tenant resides.
- Snapshots/backups: by default snapshots taken by the deployment automation are stored in the customer-owned bucket/volume when configured for BYO storage. If customers elect to use Redwood-managed snapshot escrow (rare for regulated customers), snapshots are retained for a configurable period; we can include the snapshot manifest and a deletion audit trail.
- BYO KMS: yes — when a customer provides their KMS, Redwood never stores plaintext keys. We can provide KMS event logs (rotation/deactivation) exported as redacted event streams and a signed statement that data reconstitution required those keys. For stronger proof, we can offer an HSM-backed key destruct sequence with a verifiable event record.
- Contract timelines: typical defaults we propose for Private are 0–7 days active purge, up to 30 days for any queued replication/snapshot windows, and up to 90 days in limited offsite escrow scenarios. All of these are negotiable and we can add firm SLA-backed bounds in Dedicated/Enterprise deals.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will assemble an evidence package (matrix + sample signed attestation + sample manifest) and share by end of day Monday.
2) Rishi — can you advise on firm warranty phrasing we can offer in procurement (we should not promise absolute destruction for escrowed snapshots unless contractually defined).
3) Lauren — would you like to weigh in on the maximum negotiable windows for Priority deals?

Elena / Aisha — quick legal/contract note. For procurement we can offer a "Residency & Deletion Warranty" paragraph that commits Redwood to:
- Performing the tenant wipe within X business days upon receipt of a validated request;
- Producing the deletion artifacts (manifest + run ID + signed attestation) within 3 business days of wipe completion;
- Stipulating that for any customer-provided escrow/snapshot outside of customer-owned storage, Redwood will provide deletion assistance and a certified attestation but cannot absolutely certify third-party escrow destruction unless a shared process is specified in the SOW.

Recommended placeholders for the SOW:
- "Wipe execution window: 7 business days (subject to mutual verification)."
- "Snapshot/escrow retention window: configurable, default 30 days unless otherwise agreed."
- "Evidence package delivery: within 3 business days post completion of wipe."

We should not bind ourselves to irreversible destruction of data held by a third-party escrow absent explicit contractual controls. Happy to draft a short addendum.
